nv_second_pullout_calico_ii.blurb: Second Pullout is a cluster of sandstone walls in the Calico Hills part of Red Rock Canyon, close to Las Vegas, and it works as the area's main sport hub. Bolted lines dominate by a wide margin, with a smaller collection of trad routes and almost no bouldering. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, backed by a healthy stock of 5.8 and 5.9 lines and a fair number at 5.12, with a few reaching low 5.13. Popular walls include the Black Corridor, the Great Red Book Area, the Stratocaster Area and the Gallery. Late fall and early spring are the favoured seasons, and the sandstone is fragile when wet, so it pays to let it dry after rain.

co_clear_creek_canyon_bouldering.blurb: Boulder problems are spread along the roughly fifteen miles of Clear Creek Canyon in Colorado, from near Idaho Springs down to the edge of Golden. The canyon rock is mostly gneiss and schist, and many blocks sit a short walk from the road. Everything here is bouldering, from easy V0 problems through a broad middle of V3 to V9 and on to a handful of V10 to V12 tests. The Tunnel 1 Trail Boulders are the largest cluster. Other groupings include Floyd Hill Saddleback, the Cat Slab Boulders and a gully of water-polished blocks near mile marker 268.

nv_la_madre_range.blurb: The La Madre Range is a belt of limestone cliffs and foothills on the west side of Las Vegas, wrapped around La Madre Mountain. Sport climbing is the bulk of it, with a thin scatter of trad, top-rope and bouldering. Most lines fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a good number of easier ones and a small group at 5.13. The stone ranges from chossy to solid and tends to be sharp. Lone Mountain, Cheyenne Mountain, La Madre North and the Gun Club are the largest sub-areas; La Madre North is a more secluded hillside than the eastern, town-side crags. Late fall to early spring is the best window, and the range is a cool-season fallback when Red Rock sandstone is wet.

ca_geology_tour_road.blurb: Geology Tour Road runs through the southern end of Queen Valley in Joshua Tree National Park, an eighteen-mile dirt loop that passes rock formations and a number of climbing areas. The mix is unusually even: traditional routes lead, bouldering is nearly as common, and there are some sport and top-rope lines. Boulder problems skew easy to moderate, while roped climbs mostly sit at 5.9 to 5.11 with a good spread of easier ones. The Virgin Islands area is the biggest cluster, followed by the Towers of Uncertainty, the Galapagos and the Western Belt. Queen Valley as a whole feels wild and remote, with some of the park's longer walks in.

co_east.blurb: East is the main bouldering zone around Buena Vista, Colorado, in the Arkansas River valley. Nearly every climb is a boulder problem, running from V0 to about V10, with the bulk in the V2 to V5 range and a smaller number of harder lines above that. Sleeping Indian Mountain is the largest cluster, with several faces on the mountain above the river and a set of trail and river boulders closer to the water. The 4 Mile Boulders, the Tunnel Roadside Boulders and Iron Mountain make up much of the rest. Together these hold most of the bouldering around town.

qc_03_quebec_city.blurb: Quebec City sits in a ring of crags, and the region mixes climbing styles more than most: bouldering, traditional routes and top-rope lines lead, with a smaller share of sport, plus some ice and mixed in winter. Roped grades run from easy 5.4 up to 5.13, with most routes between 5.7 and 5.12. Mont Wright, near Stoneham and under thirty minutes from the city centre, is the largest single area, mostly easy routes in hardwood forest, which makes it a common place to learn. Champlain and Le Pylône sit in the Sainte-Foy district. Montmorency Falls draws ice climbers, and its frozen face catches the sun for most of the day.
